anomalies.observed: The two series resistors that sit between the PWM source nets and the servo signal pins (J3 pin 3 / J8 pin 3) are drawn as 0 Ω in the right‑hand jumper/series network. No 1 kΩ value appears anywhere on the sheet: the only non‑zero resistor values present are 47k, 10k, 5.1k, 20k, 2k, 2.2k and 2.2k (7 values), whereas the specification calls for 9 non‑zero resistors including the two 1 kΩ series parts.
anomalies.expected: Specification §2 component table: 'R3, R4 | 1k each | Series resistors from the PWM1/PWM2 GPIO nets to J3 pin 3 / J8 pin 3 respectively.' The servo signal lines must each carry a 1 kΩ series resistor.

evidence.quote: R3, R4 | 1k each | Series resistors from the PWM1/PWM2 GPIO nets to J3 pin 3 / J8 pin 3 respectively.

Right-side resistor network (sheet /, page 1): all eight resistors in the PWM‑select / serial / series cluster (R20, R14, R4, R23, R15, R21, R17, R12) are annotated '0'; no '1k' value is drawn on the sheet.

anomalies.impact: In PWM mode the M5Stack GPIO drives the SG90‑class servo signal pin through a short (0 Ω) instead of the intended 1 kΩ buffer, removing the designed series impedance/current‑limiting on both servo signal lines; this can increase ringing/EMI and stress the GPIO and servo input, deviating from the intended buffered drive.

parsed.summary: Apart from a wholesale re‑numbering of reference designators (a labeling convention, not a behavioral change), the schematic otherwise matches the spec, but the two 1 kΩ servo‑signal series resistors (R3/R4) are drawn as 0 Ω — the sheet contains no 1 kΩ value at all — so the servo signal lines lose their intended series buffering.
